goal.title: Restyle the timeline and add turn rewind
criteria: From any line, Play from here plays on from that event, and from any line but the newest, Rewind to here rewinds to just after it.
Each turn's and each half's Rewind and Play act on its start.
The controls are visible without hovering, and at least 44px on touch devices.
With the timeline docked below, the board and timeline can be resized and the turn list jumps to any player's half.

scope.rule: Change only the files that belong to this item; change nothing that belongs to another task.

verdicts.evidence: Timeline.svelte (commit 5d77c81 diff, Timeline.svelte hunks): each line's Play button calls playFrom(l.id), which starts the replay after the previous line (startReplay(log[i-1].id)), so the first step is that event. Each line's Rewind is rendered as jump(l.id) only when l.id !== lastId, so every line except the newest has it, and it rewinds to just after the event. web/e2e/timeline.spec.js (first test, 'a line's Play from here...') exercises both. web/e2e/phone.spec.js (test 'the last timeline entry has no rewind button') checks the missing rewind on the last line.

Timeline.svelte diff: playStart = (h) => startReplay(startOf(h)) and rewindHalf = (h) => jump(startOf(h), ...). Turn headings use jump(startOf(t), ...) for Rewind and playStart(t) for Play. Setup uses startOf(t), which returns lines.at(-1).id for turn 0. startOf lives in web/src/lib/timeline.js (new file) and returns the opening-draw line after 'turn N start'. Half headings (h4) and the docked rail's half buttons use rewindHalf(h), and the rail's setup button uses jump(startOf(t), 'setup'). web/e2e/timeline.spec.js ('each turn's and each player's half's Rewind...' and '...Play replays from its start...') checks each start for both controls.

The opacity-0 rules for .acts and .rw are gone from Timeline.svelte; the remaining opacity rule is .line.ahead { opacity: 0.5 }, which is not hover-driven. Timeline.svelte's @media (pointer: coarse) block sets .acts button, .head-btn and .turn-row button to var(--touch-target), which is 44px (internal/design/tokens.css, --touch-target: 44px). PlaybackBar.svelte's coarse block sets button, button.icon and .speed select to min-width/height var(--touch-target), and the scrubber to the same height. App.svelte's coarse block sets aside .dock and .grip to var(--touch-target). web/e2e/timeline.spec.js ('the timeline's play and rewind show without a hover...') asserts full opacity on ancestors, visibility without hover, and 44px boxes on touch.

Docked resize: App.svelte diff adds a .grip with role=separator, dragDock (pointer capture, moves by the clientY delta) and keyDock (ArrowUp/Down by 16px, PageUp/PageDown by 80px, Home/End to the bounds). The height is applied via style:--dock-h on .app, and the CSS rule .body.panel.bottom uses grid-template-rows: minmax(0, 1fr) var(--dock-h). The board's --cw in .app.panel-bottom reads --dock-h, so the cards follow the split. The height is kept in memory only (app.dockHeight in web/src/lib/store.svelte.js). Turn list: Timeline.svelte renders <nav class="rail" aria-label="Turns"> when rail is set, with a button per non-setup half calling rewindHalf(h), plus prize counts from prizeScores. web/e2e/timeline.spec.js ('docked below, dragging the handle...' and 'docked below, the turn list rewinds...') covers the drag, keys, storage and half jumps. Changes outside the named files (lib/timeline.js, playback.svelte.js, store.svelte.js, tokens, desktop and phone specs, screenshot baselines) are not verdicted here.
